task: Review every supplied part, discover the most consequential events from the supplied evidence, cluster related reports, assign the best-fit broad news category dynamically and produce up to 150 processed stories using schema/processed-news.schema.json. The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

Kerala High Court suspends ex-DGP Tomin Thachankary's four-year jail sentence in DA case
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday suspended the 4-year-jail sentence of former Director General of Police (DGP) Tomin Thachankary in a disproportionate assets case [ Tomin J Thachakary v State of Kerala ]. Justice A Badharudeen pronounced the order on an application filed by Thachankary seeking suspension of his jail sentence until the High Court decides his appeal challenging the conviction. While allowing Thachankary's plea, the Court observed that, prima facie there was no error in the vigilance court's finding that he had acquired assets disproportion to his known income. However, considering that the sentence imposed on him was only four years, the Court held that it could be suspended by imposing appropriate conditions. It, thus, directed him to deposit 75% of the ₹30.84 lakh fine imposed by the vigilance court before he could be released on bail and to execute a bail bond of ₹5 lakh with two sureties within a further period of one week after depositing the fine amount. Justice A Badharudeen The Court had reserved its decision on September 24 after hearing Thachankary's plea and the objections raised by the State government. items.title: State tells Calcutta High Court Mahua Moitra given "X" category security; TMC MP disputes claim
items.summary: Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader Mahua Moitra on Wednesday disputed a claim made by the State government before the Calcutta High Court that she has been provided "X" level security as per her entitlement as a Member of Parliament (MP) [ Mahua Moitra v. State of West Bengal ]. The submission was made before Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya during the hearing of Moitra's plea for upgraded security following the Tehatta egg-pelting incident in Nadia. The Court proceeded to grant Moitra time place her submission (about the current status of her security cover) on record by filing a supplementary affidavit. The matter will be heard next on December 2. Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya During an October 7 hearing of the matter , the Court had asked the State if there were any guidelines on the security cover or protection to be given to dignitaries like MPs. At the time, Moitra's counsel had submitted that there is a "Yellow Book" which contains guidelines on how MPs should be given protection, which was a highly confidential document in the State's custody. items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday refused to grant an interim injunction against the JioStar over its upcoming movie Queen Forever [Phantom Studios v. JioStar India & Ors]. Justice Sandeep Marne declined relief to Phantom Studios, which claimed that the movie was an unauthorised sequel to the 2014 film Queen. A detailed order is awaited. Justice Sandeep Marne Phantom sued JioStar India for ₹250 crore alleging that Queen Forever breaches a 2012 co‑production agreement and a 2022 deed of novation under which Phantom and JioStar (earlier Viacom18) are claimed to be joint and equal owners of all intellectual property and derivative rights in Queen. In the interim application which Justice Marne decided today, Phantom sought an order temporarily barring the defendants from making, releasing, or promoting any sequel or adaptation of the film (including Queen Forever ) without Phantom's written permission until the suit is finally decided. JioStar denied these allegations claiming the new film is not a continuation of the original film. items.title: Homemaker’s household services cannot be ignored in accident compensation merely because she is over 70: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that while determining motor accident compensation, a homemaker’s unpaid household and caregiving services cannot be disregarded merely because she is above 70 years of age [Ganga Devi v Rajesh Kumar & Ors] . Justice Anish Dayal said that the assessment of compensation should not be founded upon stereotypes or assumptions that a person ceases to contribute merely by reason of having attained an advanced age. The Court warned against such prejudices and said that data demonstrates that women beyond the age of 70 years continue to render gratuitous services to their families, including household and caregiving services. “This Court is conscious that such contributions, particularly those rendered within the household and without monetary remuneration, are often overlooked or undervalued. However, the absence of a monetary consideration cannot operate to the advantage of the tortfeasor or diminish the compensation otherwise payable to the injured claimant,” the Bench ruled. items.title: Supreme Court laments lawyer blaming client for AI-generated fake judgments
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently criticised an advocate-on-record (AoR) for attempting to blame litigants after a compilation of judgments submitted before it was alleged to contain non-existent decisions generated using artificial intelligence (AI). [Deepak Raheja v. Omkara] A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih observed that the lawyer had attempted to shift responsibility onto the appellants while feigning ignorance of the contents of the compilation. The Court made the observations in a judgment delivered on October 15 while dismissing appeals challenging insolvency proceedings against two companies operating luxury hotels in Bengaluru and Pune. " Before parting, we wish to advert to an undesirable incident that transpired in course of hearing. On behalf of the appellants, a compilation of judgments was placed on record to which the respondents raised immediate serious objection. According to them, the compilation was replete with AI generated non-existent judgments ," the Court recorded. items.title: Turning off light, lying on woman and pressing her mouth not attempt to rape: Patna High Court
items.summary: The Patna High Court recently held that entering a woman’s house late at night, extinguishing the oil lamp, lying upon her and smothering her mouth to stifle her cries does not amount to an attempt to commit rape [ Md Ainul Haque v. State of Bihar ]. Justice Sandeep Kumar held that in the absence of any overt act towards penetration, such acts fall short of Section 376/511 ( rape/attempt to rape ) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Consequently, the High Court set aside the four-year rigorous imprisonment awarded to the accused, one Md Ainul Haque, under Sections 376/511 IPC, reducing his substantive sentence to the period of about two and a half months already spent in custody. It, however, convicted him under Section 354 IPC ( outraging modesty ) and directed him to pay a fine of ₹25,000, ordering the entire amount to be handed over to the victim as compensation. Justice Sandeep Kumar The order comes in the backdrop of a similar controversial ruling by the Patna High Court earlier this year, where the court held that pressing a woman's breasts or unfastening her salwar string did not constitute an attempt to rape. items.title: Vijay Mallya's "flamboyant lifestyle" coming in the way of settling bank claims: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Wednesday opined that former Kingfisher Airlines promoter Vijay Mallya’s “flamboyant lifestyle” appears to be hindering the closure of loan recovery proceedings pending against the now-defunct airline [ Diageo Holdings Netherlands B V & others Vs SBI & others ]. A Division Bench of Justice DK Singh and Justice T M Nadaf made the observation while granting relief to Diageo Holdings Netherlands BV in a dispute concerning shares held by Vijay Mallya in United Breweries Limited (UBL), which were pledged in connection with a loan. The Court held that Diageo's claim ranked higher than the entitlement of the banks to these shares. Notably, the Court also observed that the banks had already recovered assets worth ₹14,131.6 crore against the ₹6,203-crore loan given to Kingfisher Airlines. The Court, therefore, held that the banks were not justified in staking a claim over UBL shares as well. " When the Consortium of Banks’ claim for their dues against the loan of INR 6,203 crores has got almost settled by making recovery of assets worth more than INR 14,131.6 crores, there would be no justification for their claim over the UBL shares," the Court held. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday said it would petitions challenging the validity of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, including pleas for further interim relief, on November 4. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi briefly heard the matter today, when concerns were raised about the changing status of waqf properties while the case continues to remain pending. Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi Notably, in September 2025, another Bench of the Court had granted limited interim relief , staying some provisions of the Act but allowing the operation of several other key provisions to continue. Senior Advocate Rauf Rahin , today urged the Court to fix a date for hearing the matter as the Act's continued operation was giving rise to serious consequences. " The Limitation Act, they say, would now become applicable. So Waqf properties, if they are not defined within that period, would be affected immediately. Waqf-by-user is also being affected. An interim order was passed about one and a half years back. If the matters are not heard, the consequences would be serious. I only request a date," he said. items.title: J&K High Court stays CAT Jammu order imposing ₹10,000 costs on senior advocate
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh has stayed the operation of an order passed by the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), Jammu Bench, imposing costs of ₹10,000 on Senior Advocate Jahangir Ganai. A Division Bench of Justices Sanjeev Kumar and MA Chowdhary passed the interim order while hearing the senior advocate’s writ petition against the Tribunal’s order. Justice Sanjeev Kumar and Justice M A Choudhary The CAT had imposed the costs after recording that Ganai appeared before it during virtual proceedings without wearing uniform and made derogatory remarks against it. The Tribunal had also observed that he appeared to be unapologetic about appearing without uniform. After hearing counsel for the parties, the High Court observed that “the case for indulgence at this stage is made out.” The Division Bench expressed its intention to mediate and explore an amicable settlement. The Court directed the tribunal members concerned and the petitioners to appear in person before it in chambers on October 21. “In the meanwhile, there shall be stay of the effect and operation of the impugned order,” the High Court directed. items.title: J&K High Court says doctors hesitant to perform abortions without court order, aggrieved mothers left at God's mercy
items.summary: The Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court recently observed that doctors refuse to perform abortions even in cases where the procedure is legally permitted under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act. Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani made the comment while dealing with a case of a woman who, despite serious foetal abnormalities, had to approach the Court for medical termination of pregnancy after doctors refused to perform abortion without judicial order. The Court emphasised that medical practitioners should not unnecessarily avoid attending emergent cases for which statutory directions under the MTP Act and relevant rules are clear. "The registered medical practitioners especially doctors working in the associated hospitals of medical colleges and in other district hospitals do not shoulder their statutory responsibilities in terms of the provisions of Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 and the rules of 2003 framed thereunder in justified cases thereby leaving the aggrieved mothers at the mercy of the God who, in search of some solace feel constrained to shoulder further mental agony and burden of approaching the courts of law for legal directions," the Court said. items.title: “They don't take this seriously?” Supreme Court on Centre's failure to respond to plea for strict age checks at liquor outlets
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday expressed concern over the Union government's failure to appear in the hearing of a plea seeking mandatory age verification at liquor outlets across the country, despite the service of notice [ Community Against Drunken Driving Versus The Union Of India And Ors. ]. A Bench of Justice Vikram Nath , Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh heard the matter briefly today, when it noted that no counsel had appeared for the Central government despite service of notice. “Respondent 1 (the Union Government) notice is served. Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh The Court proceeded to grant the Union government four weeks to file its response. The Bench also said that it would request the Solicitor General of India, Tushar Mehta to appear in the matter. items.title: Property acquired by Catholic priests after joining religious order belongs to society, not legal heirs: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court has held that properties acquired by Catholic priests after entering a religious order and undertaking religious vows belong to the religious society concerned and cannot be claimed by their legal heirs merely on the basis of their family relationship [ ABVM Vs Deiva Nayagan ]. A Division Bench of Justices N Anand Venkatesh and KK Ramakrishnan passed the ruling while allowing appeals filed by a Catholic religious society against a district court order granting succession rights to the relatives of a deceased priest over fixed deposits worth ₹56 lakh. The Court held that the ownership of properties acquired during a priest's religious service must be determined in light of the obligations undertaken by the priest and the circumstances of the property's acquisition. " The legal consequence of such acquisition must therefore be determined in the light of the religious obligations undertaken by him and the institutional character in which those properties were acquired, rather than merely by the fact that the title documents stood in his individual name," the judgment said. items.title: Add photos, videos of illegal modifications while uploading accident vehicle reports: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has directed the Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) to ensure that photographs and videos of of illegal modifications to vehicles involved in accidents must be part of the accident reports uploaded on the Electronic Detailed Accident Report (e-DAR) portal [ Suo Motu v Union of India & Ors ]. Justices Anil K Narendran and Muralee Krishna S gave the directions on October 8, 2026, while considering a suo motu case dealing with road safety and unauthorised modification of vehicles in Kerala. " We deem it appropriate to direct (the Transport Commissioner), through the concerned Deputy Transport Commissioners, to ensure that vehicle modification details with photographs and videos of vehicles involved in accidents are uploaded through e-DAR portal (www.irad.parivahan.gov.in), by the concerned inspecting officers, " the Court said. Inspecting officers must upload details of any violation of safety standards that raise the risk of injury to the person hit by or brushing against the bodywork of such vehicles, the Court added.
